title_he: הוֹי עוֹבְרֵי דֶרֶךְ, הַגִּידוּ אָנָה תֵּלֵכוּ
review: The hymn is the pilgrims' dialogue: 1:1–8 is Isa 35:8–10 with Ps 84:6–8 and Rev 7:17, 2:1–8 is Matt 11:28 with Isa 55:1 and Luke 14:23.

The print's second stanza sets the invitation in quotation marks from line 6 onward; the Hebrew keeps the colon at 2:6 and lets the last two lines be the voice, rather than importing quotation marks into the lines.

1:5–6 keep the two-stage geography of the Arabic (الْقِفَار then صَوْبَ أَفْرَاحِ الْخُلُود): the Hebrew uses יְשִׁימוֹן, the wilderness name of Deut 32:10 and Ps 107:4, so the road is a real desert and not a metaphor for difficulty.
